root_idea.summary: The root centers on the idea of an edge, boundary, or defined side, with related branches of turning aside and measuring or delimiting.
root_idea.development: From the notion of an edge or side, the sources develop senses of adopting one mode or position, turning something away from its proper direction, altering speech, and measuring a wound. Livelihood and deprivation usages are recorded as separate lexical branches.

senses.definition: To turn words or speech away from their proper meanings or places; to distort or alter their wording.
senses.usage_conditions: In the Quranic usage, the object is words or speech. The alteration may involve changing wording or presenting it in a form that permits divergent interpretations.
In the Quranic expression عَلَى حَرْفٍ, the noun retains the image of standing at an edge or outer side.

senses.definition: A single side, mode, or condition on which one proceeds.
senses.usage_conditions: In عَلَى حَرْفٍ, the expression describes conditional, unstable adherence: remaining committed in favorable circumstances but turning away when tested or distressed.

senses.definition: Turning aside in battle in order to return and fight; using a tactical maneuver rather than fleeing.
senses.usage_conditions: Used with لِقِتَالٍ for a combatant who withdraws or shifts position as a stratagem of warfare.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To turn a thing away from its proper way or manner; to alter it.
To earn or seek subsistence for one's household, including by applying oneself to a craft.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The construction may specify earning for one's family or earning with one's hands.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To apply collyrium to the eye with a ميل.
To suffer the loss of some property.
To turn hearts away, make them aloof, or remove their confidence.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Recorded in the expression يُحَرِّفُ القُلُوبَ and in a reported phrase concerning a pestilence.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To cut the nib of a writing reed obliquely.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The result is a nib whose two teeth are unequal in height.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Putting something into motion or a state of commotion; in a specific gesture, moving the hand as if cutting with the edge of a sword.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The hand-motion sense belongs to a reported expression and is not a general restriction on the verb.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To be debarred from the means of subsistence, or to have one's earnings turned away and one's livelihood made difficult.
Vying with another for superiority in glory, or dealing with another in contest or interaction.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The expression may be understood in relation to warfare, occupation, lineage, or requital according to its context.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To requite someone for good or evil, or to recompense someone for an act.
Measuring a wound with a probe.
To have one's property or cattle increase and become prosperous or sound in condition.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The subject is a person's property or livestock.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To emaciate or render a she-camel lean.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This usage is attributed to one authority, while another reading is reported as حَرَثَ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To turn aside, away, toward, or against; to become altered from one's proper course.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: It can also describe a temperament becoming disordered; direction and attitude are determined by the accompanying preposition or context.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A sharp summit, ridge, brow, ledge, or projecting portion of a mountain.
The obliquely cut nib of a writing reed.
Either of the two lateral halves of the head.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used in the plural expression حَرْفَا الرَّأْسِ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A letter of the alphabet.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The plural is حُرُوفٌ or أَحْرُفٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A grammatical particle that expresses a meaning without being a noun or a verb.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is the technical grammatical use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A word.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This broader usage is recorded as a lexical extension of the term.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A dialect, idiom, or mode of expression associated with a group of Arabs; a particular manner of reading or expression.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The expression نَزَلَ القُرْآنُ عَلَى سَبْعَةِ أَحْرُفٍ is explained in terms of dialects or modes of reading.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A she-camel described as lean, light, strong, swift, or effective in pace; it may also be described as large or high-bred.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The word is explicitly applied to a she-camel, not to a male camel. The sources preserve differing comparisons with the edge of a mountain, a sword, or an alphabetic letter.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Ill-fatedness, deprivation of prosperity, or being denied the means of subsistence.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: It may describe lack of increase in property or cattle and the distress associated with lacking a means of livelihood.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A pungent grain resembling mustard, commonly identified with garden cress or a similar seed.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The singular grain is treated as a noun of unity with ـة.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A craft, handicraft, occupation, or habitual work by which a person earns a livelihood.
A seller of الحُرْف, the pungent grain identified with حَبُّ الرَّشَادِ.
A fellow-worker in one's craft or ordinary occupation; an associate.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: In later foreign usage it can mean a drinking companion or serve as an angry or vituperative form of address.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The quality of burning or biting the tongue; acridity or pungency.
Something burning or biting to the tongue, such as an onion or another pungent food.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The cited form is حِرِّيفٌ, not حَرِّيفٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A place to which one can turn away or back from a matter.
A place where a person earns or seeks subsistence and pursues an occupation.
A person whose property or cattle increases and becomes prosperous or sound in condition.
One whose property has gone or been lost.
A writing reed whose nib has been cut obliquely, with one tooth higher than the other.
One who turns, inclines, moves, or removes hearts; an epithet applied to God.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The alternatives reflect closely related descriptions of directing or changing the state of hearts.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A probe used to measure the depth of a wound.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The plural forms include مَحَارِيفُ and مَحَارِفُ according to the cited analyses.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A person deprived of good fortune or prosperity, whose earnings are insufficient or whose livelihood is withheld.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The term can include one who earns with his hands but not enough to support himself or his household.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A handicraftsman or worker with his hands.

lane_unit_coverage.note: Form I alteration and the Quran-attested derived alteration of words are both covered.
The hand-sign expression is covered under the motion and gesture use.
Being deprived or straitened in livelihood.
Vying, dealing, or contesting with another.
Increase and improvement of property or cattle.
Attributed use for rendering a she-camel lean.
Turning aside, toward, or against and becoming disordered.
Physical edge senses, the Quranic idiom, and its classical specializations are covered.
Dialect or mode of reading and expression.
Later foreign usages are included in the usage conditions of the associate entry.
Acridity or burning of the tongue.
A place to turn away or back.
A place of earning or occupational pursuit.
Property having gone or been lost.
A reed with an obliquely cut nib.
Person denied prosperity or sufficient livelihood.

cautions: The Quranic noun حَرْفٌ in 22:11 occurs in the idiom عَلَى حَرْفٍ; its literal edge image and its conditional or unstable stance are therefore presented as related but distinct senses.
